8587.t: BM2213: Analog and Digital Electronics for Bioengineers
8587.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM2213 : Analog and Digital Electronics for Bioengineers { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Basics of Electronics, Analog Electronics basics, Introduction to amplifier, Need of amplifier and types of amplifiers, Biopotential amplifier block diagram,
TYPES OF BIOPOTENTIAL AMPLIFIERS
Basic requirements of Bio-potential Amplifiers. Problems encountered in Bio amplifiers- Frequency distortion, Artifacts from electric transients, Interference from electric devices.
Right Leg driven amplifiers-and its need. Bio-potential amplifiers-Instrumentation and Differential, Common Mode Rejection Ratio
Problems: Gain, Slew Rate. Amplifiers for Medical applications. Analog active filters- Low pass, High pass, Band pass, Notch Filter. Filter applications-Anti-aliasing, SNR Improvement.
Basic digital logic circuits, Combinational logic circuit, Half and Full adder, Comparator, Code Converters, Multiplexers and Demultiplexers, Encoders and Decoders. Basic Architectural Distinctions between Combinational and Sequential circuits, Sequential logic circuits, Flip-Flops, Conversion from one type of Flipflop to another, Timing. Digital Interfaces- ADC types-Tracking and Successive Approximation, Flash ADC.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce fundamental principles of analog and digital electronics commonly used in biomedical research.
2 .

To familiarize the basic electronic circuits, techniques and considerations for the development of biomedical devices.
3 .

To understand the role of Electronics in Bio medical instrument development.
4 .

To impart familiarity with the design and implementation of different types of practically used sequential circuits.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Have a thorough understanding of the fundamental concepts and techniques used in analog electronics.
2. The ability to understand the fundamental concept of digital electronics, analyze and design various combinational and sequential circuits.
3. Ability to identify basic requirements for a design application related to biomedical systems.
4. To develop skills to realize, build, and troubleshoot analog biomedical circuits, instruments.
5. To understand the practical circumstance of biomedical devices analog and digital circuits importance.

Essential Reading

1 .

Robert B. Northrop, Analysis and Application of Analog Electronic Circuits to Biomedical Instrumentation, CRC Press , Taylor & Francis Group , 2nd Edition

2 .

John G. Webster, Medical Instrumentation: Application and Design, John Wiley & Sons Inc. , 4th Edition

Supplementary Reading

1 .

David. A. Bell, Electronic Devices and Circuits, Oxford University Press , 5th Edition

2 .

Robert L. Boylestad, Louis Nashelsky, Electronic Devices and Circuit, Pearson Education, India , 11th Edition

7819.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM3602 : Biomedical Instrumentation - II { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Arrhythmia and Cardiac Equipment's (Hours 8)
ECG morphology - Normal and Abnormal Waves, Heart rate variability, heart rate monitor, Holter Monitor, Phonocardiography, Cardiac Pacemaker-Internal, and External Pacemaker, Types of pacemakers, Pacemaker codes.
Module 2: Patient Monitoring and Respiratory Measurements (Hours 8)
Blood Pressure: indirect methods - Auscultatory and Oscillometric method, direct methods. Patient monitoring systems. Spirometer-Lung Volume and vital capacity, measurements of residual volume.
Module 3: Ultrasound in biomedical applications (Hours 7)
Basics principles of ultrasound and echo techniques, display techniques of Ultrasound- A, B and M mode, Application of ultrasound as a diagnostic tool – Echocardiogram, Echoencephalogram.
Module 4: Flow meters and cardiac output (Hours 7)
Blood flow meter- Electromagnetic and Ultrasonic types, Cardiac Output measurement methods.
Module 5: Patient Safety, Codes and Standards (Hours 6)
Physiological effects of electricity, Macro shock, and Micro shock hazards – Patient’s electrical environment –Electrical safety codes and standards
.

Course Objective

1 .

To Understand the medical devices applied in physiological measurements
2 .

To Know the ultrasound imaging technique and its use in diagnosis
3 .

To understand the principles of pressure and flow measurements
4 .

To understand the patient safety in hospital environment

Course Outcome

1 .

After completing the course, the students will able to:
1. Explain about measurements of electrical and non electrical parameters of physiological measurements
2. Describe the different morphology and arrhythmia condition of ECG signal
3. discuss the applications of Ultrasound and electromagnetic field in biomedical field
4. understand the cardiovascular mechanism and measurement methods
5. Outline the importance of patient safety against electrical hazard

Essential Reading

1 .

John G. Webster, Medical Instrumentation application and design, John Wiley and Sons

2 .

Khandpur R.S, Hand-book of Biomedical Instrumentation, Tata McGraw Hill

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Carr, Joseph J, Brown, John.M, Introduction to Biomedical equipment technology, John Wiley and Sons

2 .

Leslie Cromwell, Fred J, Weibell, Erich A, Pfeiffer, Biomedical Instrumentation and Measurements, Prentice-Hall India

7307.t: BM6231: Computational Methods in Biomedical Engineering
7307.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6231 : Computational Methods in Biomedical Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I
Introduction to computation, mathematical modelling – analytical and numerical method, mathematical tools, application in biomedical engineering.
Module II
Systems of linear and non-linear equations, Cramer's rule, Gauss elimination, Gauss Jordan, LU decomposition, Gauss-Seidel method, iterative solution techniques. Eigen values and eigen vectors, power iteration methods. Algebraic Equations – bisection method, Newton-Raphson and secant method.
Module III
System of ODE and nonlinear ODE, partial differential equations (PDE), classification of PDE – elliptic equations, parabolic equations (transient diffusion equation), hyperbolic equations (wave equation), numerical differentiation and integration, Taylor’s series, Picard’s method, Euler’s method, Runge Kutta and Milne’s method, trapezoidal method, Simpson's method, quadrature method, explicit and implicit schemes, finite difference method, finite volume method, concept of finite element method, solution of Laplace’s and Poisson’s equations, solution of heat transfer equation.
Module IV
Problems in biomechanics and biomaterials, inverse problems in the field of biomedical imaging.

Course Objective

1 .

To become familiar with concept of computation in biomedical engineering
2 .

To learn various method of solving linear and non-linear equations
3 .

To learn various method of solving ODE and PDE
4 .

To review computational problems in biomedical engineering

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course the student will be able to:
CO1: Apply suitable methods for mathematical modelling
CO2: Solve linear and non-linear equations using iterative methods
CO3: Apply various numerical methods for solving an equation
CO4: Develop a computational solution to the ODE/PDE
CO5: Develop solution for problems in biomedical engineering

Essential Reading

1 .

Gupta S.K., Numerical Methods for Engineers, New Age International

2 .

Chapra S.C. and Canale R.P., Numerical Methods for Engineers, McGraw Hill , 2006

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Joe D Hoffman, Numerical Methods for Engineers and Scientists, Marcel Dekker , 2001

2 .

T. Veerarajan and T. Ramachandran, Numerical methods with programs in C, Tata McGraw-Hill , 2006

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH2410 : Fuels and Combustion { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Solid fuels: Coal origin, Chemical composition, Calorific value, Classifications, Characteristics and Distribution of Indian coals, Coal storage, Coal washing and blending, Petrographic constituents of coal, Carbonization of coal, Manufacture and properties of metallurgical coke, Recovery of byproducts Liquid fuels: Origin and composition of crude oil, distillation of crude oil and properties of gasoline, kerosene and diesel oil, Breaking and rebuilding processes like Cracking, Reforming, Polymerization, Coal tar distillation, Shale oil Gaseous fuels: Natural gas, Coal gas, Coke oven and blast furnace gas, Manufacture of water gas and producer gas, Carbureted water gas Synthetic fuels: Hydrogenation of coal, Fischer-Tropsch synthesis Introduction to nuclear fuels and nuclear reactors Combustion of solid fuels, Calorific values, Adiabatic flame temperatures, Combustion calculations, Gas analysis, Furnace design.

Course Objective

1 .

The basic course objective is to acquaint students with the fundamental properties of solid liquid and gaseous fuels and their industrial applications and designing furnaces for combustion processes.

Course Outcome

1 .

To provide an overview of different fossil fuels and stoichiometric calculations on fuel air mixtures. It would enable students to understand the significance of combustion in various process industries. Additionally, it aims at equipping students to design industrial furnaces and boilers.

Essential Reading

S. Sarkar, Fuels and Combustion, Universities Press , 2009

2 .

S.R. Turns, An Introduction to Combustion: Concepts and Applications, McGraw Hill Education , 2012

Supplementary Reading

J. Brame and King, Fuels: Solid, liquid and gaseous fuels, Kessinger Publishing, LLC , 2007

2 .

A.I. Levorsen, Geology of Petroleum, CBS , 2004

7563.t: EE6441: Wind and Solar Energy Systems
7563.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6441 : Wind and Solar Energy Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module1:
Sources of Energy: Renewable energy sources and features. Introduction to wind and solar energy. Wind Energy: General theories of wind machines: Basic laws and concept of aerodynamics, efficiency limit for wind energy conversion. Description and performances of horizontal axis wind turbine: Design of the blades and determination of forces acting on the wind power plant, power ~ speed and torque ~ speed characteristics of wind turbines, wind turbine control systems. Description and performances of vertical axis wind turbine. (8 hrs)
Module 2:
Conversion to electrical power: Induction and synchronous generators, grid connected and self-excited induction generator operation, generation schemes with variable speed turbines, constant voltage and constant frequency generation with power electronic control, Optimized control of induction generators and synchronous generators. Reactive power compensation, Types of converters, Type of wind energy conversion system, MPPT techniques for wind electrical systems. (8 hrs)
Module 3:
Solar Energy: Solar processes and spectral composition of solar radiation Radiation flux at the Earth’s surface, solar collectors, types and performance characteristics, applications. Solar Photovoltaic systems: Operating principle, photovoltaic cell concepts, cell, module, array, series and parallel connections. Basics of Batteries: Types and parameters of batteries for PV systems, series and parallel connections and performance characteristics. (8 hrs)
Module 4:
Solar PV system design and grid integration, charge controllers, PV MPPT techniques. Applications: General overview, Distributed generation, Hybrid energy systems: Wind-Diesel hybrid system, Wind-solar hybrid system, System with energy storage, Special purpose applications. (8 hrs)
Module 5:
Wind and Solar Energy System Economics: Overview of economic assessment, capital, operation and maintenance costs of wind and solar energy systems, comparison of alternative energy systems using life cycle cost analysis. (4 hrs)

Course Objective

1 .

Explain the concept of wind and solar energy systems
2 .

To provide the students a deep insight in to the integration of power electronics converters with PV and wind energy sources.
3 .

To expose students to study various maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques of wind and PV energy systems
4 .

Explains the need for hybrid energy systems and issues associated with it.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to
1. Understand the basics of wind and solar energy conversion and their operating characteristics
2. Understand the aerodynamics of wind rotor and design the wind turbine system
3. Analyse the use of different power electronics converters and electrical machines used in standalone wind energy conversion systems
4. Understand and apply the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques for wind and PV systems
5. Design the standalone and grid connected solar PV systems.
6. Interpret the working of different configurations of hybrid energy system and life cycle cost analysis.

Essential Reading

1 .

S. N. Bhadra, D. Kastha, S. Banerjee, Wind Electrical Systems, Oxford Univ. Press , 2005

2 .

C.S. Solanki, Solar Photovoltaics Fundamentals, Technologies and Applications, PHI Learning Pvt. Ltd. , 2016

Supplementary Reading

1 .

M.G. Simoes, F.A. Farret, Alternative Energy Systems: Design and Analysis with Induction Generators, CRC Press , 2004

2 .

Nicola Femia, Giovanni Petrone, Giovanni Spagnuolo, Massimo Vitelli, Power Electronics And Control Techniques For Maximum Energy Harvesting In Photovoltaic Systems, CRC Press , 2012

Journal and Conferences

1 .

M. G. Villalva, J. R. Gazoli and E. R. Filho, "Comprehensive Approach to Modeling and Simulation of Photovoltaic Arrays," in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 24, no. 5, pp. 1198-1208, May 2009, doi: 10.1109/TPEL.2009.2013862.
2 .
